about: Every fixture of this folder. A file under good/ must validate against 'schema'. A file under bad/ must be refused, and 'rule' says which rule it breaks; 'expect' names the schema keyword that refuses it and the place in the fixture where it does (a JSON Pointer, '' for the whole value). Files named c* were captured from the daemon by capture_today.py; files named h* and b* were written by hand.

fixtures.shows: An engine asked to run a command. One surface has shown it; nobody has answered.
The owner approved it on the surface that showed it.
A tool input that holds accented text and a fraction. input_json carries it as an escaped JSON string, so the effect still fits the restricted canonical form.
A plugin asked to carry out an effect. The effect is the gate's own canonical object; it belongs to no turn.
Nobody answered before the deadline. Expired means denied; nobody is recorded as having answered.
The owner refused a plugin effect. A veto is final for that digest.
An approved effect was carried out. It can never be used again.
Two surfaces showed it; the answer came from the phone.
What the daemon keeps to route the answer to the engine's own pending request. Never sent.

fixtures.rule: A 'pending' request has no answer yet.
An 'approved' request names who approved it.
An engine acting with a session token can never answer an approval.
A plugin can never answer an approval.
A 'denied' request carries the answer 'deny'.
A tool's input rides in input_json, the exact string the digest binds, not as a loose object.
input_json is printable ASCII: text outside it is written as a \u escape.
Every display entry says whether it is trusted.
An approval id starts with 'apr-': an engine's own request id is not one.
A new canonical form is a new name in the schema, never a silent change.
No credential appears in an approval.
An 'expired' request was answered by nobody.
A plugin effect is in whole minor units.
An engine tool call always belongs to a run.
A request is shown by the CLI, the terminal client, the page or the phone page.
The private binding holds ids only.

fixtures.shows: A cursor that has read nothing yet: seq 0.
A cursor on the log of a run that was started without a session: the log is named 'run:<run_id>'.
The engine works in the launch folder itself.
The engine works in a git worktree cut from base_ref.
A decided route: engine, model, and the connection it is billed through.
A paired device. The id is a label, never the device token.

fixtures.rule: seq is never below 0.
session_id names a log: 'ses-...' or 'run:<run_id>'. A bare run id is neither.
A cursor always carries the epoch it was read in.
In 'worktree' mode worktree_path is a string.
In 'direct' mode worktree_path is null.
A principal is a kind and a label. Nothing else may ride in it.
A timestamp has exactly three decimal places and a Z.
A timestamp is UTC, written with Z, never with an offset.
An id holds no line break. Some regular expression engines let '$' match before a final newline, so the schema refuses it separately.
connection is '<kind>:<label>'. An object with a key in it is not a connection id.

fixtures.shows: Today's path as a version 2 driver: one prompt, input closed, read to the result. Every flag is false.
A driver that keeps a worker between turns, takes input mid-turn, and bridges permission prompts. It cannot fork.
A driver that can resume a conversation in a new run but keeps no worker.
One input of a turn.
The core's answer to the engine's own permission request.
End the worker's input.
What start is given. The environment is handed over separately and is in no record.
What start gives back, before the engine has reported its own session id.
A draft from parse: a usage payload exactly as event.v1 has it.
A draft from parse: a span of output.
A fork asked of a driver that cannot fork. Nothing happened before this answer.
What fork takes.

fixtures.rule: Every flag is always present: an absent flag is not false.
A new capability is a new flag in the schema.
Input in the middle of a turn needs a worker that keeps its input open.
This is the declaration of a version 2 driver.
send takes a user message, an approval answer, or close.
The engine gets 'approve' or 'deny' and nothing else.
Every user message belongs to a turn.
close carries nothing.
A driver never drafts an approval request: it asks the approval queue, and the core writes the event.
A draft payload obeys event.v1: unknown is null, never 0.
The environment is never in a record.
A missing capability is refused 'unsupported'.

fixtures.shows: A run changed state in the registry. registry_seq is the outbox row of that change, so replay matches the registry exactly.
A session was created: from is null, and the event belongs to no run and no turn.
A span of the engine's output file, with its byte offsets. Engine content is untrusted.
The engine asked to use a tool. The input is the tool's own shape and is untrusted; its digest is typed.
A tool result that carries its output as text.
A large tool result: the text is not in the log; output_ref names where it was put.
Only the core writes this event. A surface opens its approval state on it and on nothing an engine printed.
An approval left 'pending'.
Token counts read from the engine's typed stream. The cost is not reported, so it is null, not 0.
Nothing is known about this turn's usage: every number is null and the quality says so.
A running total for the engine's session, known only as a lower bound, with a modelled cost. A ledger must not add it to earlier events.
A typed plan limit on the whole connection, with the time it may clear.
A short fence on one model; when it clears is not known.
A turn produced its result.
A core event that carries engine text in 'detail': written by the core, marked untrusted.
Events 3 to 9 cannot be given. The gap event takes their place and carries seq 9.
A turn began, with the input as it was sent.
A turn reached a final state.
A message was queued for the session; the text is in the queue item, not in the log.
The queued message reached the engine inside the turn in progress.
An interrupt of a turn was asked.
The driver has no cancel, so the interrupt was delivered by stopping the run.
A Stop of one run, and who asked.
The answer of that Stop: the payload is a stop.result.v1 record.
The workspace changed.
A checkpoint of the workspace was taken.
A new session was forked from this one at a turn.
Routing chose a route because the user named it.
The log of a run started with run.start and no session is named 'run:<run_id>'.

fixtures.rule: The first event of a log is 1.
A type has a payload schema or it is not a type. A lane that needs one asks for it.
Content from an engine is always 'untrusted'.
Only the core writes approval.requested: engine output that imitates one cannot open an approval.
A number that is not known is null, never 0.
Numbers that are 'known' came from somewhere: provenance is not 'unavailable'.
Each type has exactly one payload shape.
Payloads are closed: consumer data never rides in an untyped field.
time is RFC 3339 UTC with exactly three decimal places.
time is a string, not Unix seconds.
Exactly one of text and output_ref is not null.
Exactly one of text and output_ref is not null.
When scope is 'model', model is a string.
A replay gap gives one of the listed reasons.
turn_id is always present; it is null for an event that belongs to no turn.
session_id names a log: 'ses-...' or 'run:<run_id>'.
A stop.result payload is a stop.result.v1 record, proof and all.
Engine output always belongs to a run.
turn.started names its turn.
A token count is 0 or more.
A principal is a kind and a label, here too.
A state is a lower-case word.
source is core, engine, plugin or client.

fixtures.shows: A turn in progress.
An approval is pending: a person must answer it on a surface that draws approvals.
The turn ended with a result.
The turn failed with a typed code.
The Stop was confirmed. 'cancelled' is never shown before that.
A cancel was asked and the Stop is not confirmed: still working, with cancel_requested true.
Work started with run.start: the Task id is the run id and there is no turn.
A run whose start failed.

fixtures.rule: A 'completed' Task carries its result.
'cancelled' is shown only after the Stop is confirmed.
'input_required' names the approval that is pending.
A Task that is still working has no result.
A 'failed' Task says why, with a typed code.
A pending cancel is the flag cancel_requested, not a status.
A Task derived from a turn names the turn.
A result with a code is a failure, not 'completed'.
An approval is never answered through a Task.

fixtures.shows: A message waiting for the current turn to end.
A steer message the user edited twice before it was delivered: revision 3.
Delivery has begun: from here on the item cannot be edited or withdrawn.
Delivered, with the turn it went into.
Withdrawn before delivery.

fixtures.rule: A delivered item names the turn it went into.
An item that is still queued has no turn.
A queued message has text.
delivery is 'next_turn' or 'steer'.
An item is queued, delivering, delivered or cancelled.
Every item carries its revision, so an edit from a stale client is refused.
The record is closed.

fixtures.shows: Captured: the stored record of a run started with a client_key, while it runs.
Captured: the stored record after a Stop that could not be confirmed. Its stop object carries the cgroup and marker the request was sent to.
Captured: the stored record of a stopped run, with today's 'empty' attestation.
Captured: a run that finished on its own. The store still says 'running'; only the public view says 'ended'.
Captured: a start for an engine with no route. The engine name is kept as given.
A stored record that carries every optional addition of version 1, and a start key with a request identity.
The launch intent: written before the starter is called, so there is no cgroup yet.
A Stop that arrived before the launch was recorded: kept as an intent, not sent, with no cgroup of its own.
A stopped run whose attestation is lane STOP's removal proof.

fixtures.rule: 'stopped' is stored only with an attestation.
Only a stopped record carries an attestation.
proof is 'empty' or 'removed'. Any other proof is not evidence of a stop.
'ended' is a word of the public view. The registry never stores it.
The record is closed: a lane that needs a field asks for it; it does not add labels.
Every stored record carries its generation.
The start key holds the digest of the prompt, never the prompt.
A version 1 addition is absent or has a value; it is never null.
A stopped record lists no members: they were proved gone.
The budget names a reservation and a cap. It never carries or names a key.
A run id is 1 to 64 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ and -.

fixtures.shows: Captured: the 'run' in the answer of run.start.
Captured: run.status of a running run, with the tail of its output.
Captured: one entry of run.list. A list entry carries no output.
Captured: run.status while a Stop is pending.
Captured: run.status of a stopped run.
Captured: run.status of a run that finished on its own: 'ended', recorded_state 'running', the whole route result.
Captured: the run.list entry of that run: the result is cut to status, code and detail.
Captured: run.status of a start that failed: no unit was ever recorded, so observed is null.
Captured: a unit the manager can no longer observe reads 'unknown', never 'running'.
Captured: a run of an earlier boot reads 'lost_reboot'.
The daemon's own registry could not be read: observed says so and guesses nothing.
The output file exists and could not be read: the answer names the error instead of inventing lines.
A run view that carries the version 1 additions.

fixtures.rule: When the view shows 'ended', 'lost_reboot' or 'unknown', recorded_state keeps the stored word.
recorded_state appears only when state was replaced by an observation.
A unit row carries both 'unit' and 'stop_requested'.
result is the whole route result (run.status) or exactly status, code and detail (run.list).
The output tail holds at most 50 lines.
Every view carries 'observed', null when no unit was ever recorded.
A view that says 'stopped' rests on a proof the schema knows.
The public states are the five stored ones and ended, lost_reboot and unknown.

fixtures.shows: A session that was just started: idle, no turn yet, no worker.
A multi-turn driver: three turns share one run_id, because one worker stays alive between turns. The third is in progress.
Idle, with a worker that is alive: a persistent worker waiting for input. 'idle' does not mean 'no unit'.
A driver without multi_turn: each turn has its own run, and no worker is kept between turns.
A fork: it names its parent, works in its own worktree and carries a dollar cap.
A child session whose Stop is not confirmed: it stays stop_pending, keeps its worker, and starts no new turn.
An ended session. One turn failed before it was bound to a run; one was still queued when the session ended.

fixtures.rule: A root session has no parent.
A fork or a child names its parent.
A 'live' session names the turn in progress.
An 'idle' session has no turn in progress.
An 'ended' session keeps no worker.
A running turn has not ended.
A turn in a final state says when it ended.
A session's token never appears in a record.
A turn is queued, running, interrupted, ended, failed or stopped.
A session id starts with 'ses-'.

A session belongs to a tenant.
A 'live' session has a worker: a turn in progress runs in a unit.

fixtures.shows: Captured: a Stop whose unit did not go away: pending, with the reason.
Captured: the Stop that confirmed it. repeat is true because a Stop had already been asked.
Captured: a Stop of a run that is already stopped.
Captured: a first Stop that was confirmed at once.
A Stop as lane STOP will answer it: the removal proof, the containment level, and the key of the sentence to show.
The cleanup layer raised, and the answer could not be written either: 'not recorded' is its own fact.
A Stop that carries today's proof, 'empty', in the answer itself.

fixtures.rule: A 'stopped' answer has no reason: a reason is why a Stop is NOT confirmed.
A 'pending' answer always says why.
code and state are the same word.
Nothing is attested while a Stop is pending.
The 'removed' proof names the cgroup directory by device and inode and says when it was gone.
A client that meets a proof it does not know treats the run as not stopped; the schema refuses it.
A pending reason is one of the listed words or cleanup_error:<Name>.
A surface shows only a sentence whose key is listed; it never writes its own.
The 'empty' proof carries no device, inode or removal time.
A 'stopped' answer says whether a Stop had been asked before.

fixtures.shows: The line for an engine.output event: the payload's text, sanitised, still untrusted, nothing announced.
The line for a state.changed event: state is the event's 'to'.
The line for a turn.started event: the input as sent.
The line for an approval.requested event. Only this line, from the core, moves focus to the approval.
The line for a tool.call event: a sentence the core's renderer wrote from typed fields; still untrusted because the name came from the engine.
The line for a stop.result event: state is its code, and the condition is announced.
The line for a replay.gap event.
A line may have no text: the event is in the transcript, and a plain reader prints nothing for it.

fixtures.rule: A line whose content came from an engine is untrusted.
Only an approval.requested line moves focus to the approval.
An approval.requested line comes from the core, trusted, or it is not one.
state is null unless the event reports a state.
A state.changed line carries the new state.
time_rel_ms counts up from the first event of the log.
The transcript is a projection: it has time_rel_ms and event_type, not the event's time and type.
An engine.output line carries the payload's text.
focus is one of the listed places, or null.
